heading: INT. DRAINED PUBLIC SWIMMING BATH - DAWN

units.text: INT. DRAINED PUBLIC SWIMMING BATH - DAWN
The great pool lies empty, its blue tiles cracked into a map of rivers nobody named.
Pigeons stitch through the rafters, and the light from the broken skylight lies in long pale planks across the deep end, where a lifeguard's chair still stands, lashed with rust.

MARGUERITE LAVOISIER (70s, white braid to her waist, a swimmer's shoulders gone soft) sits on the lip of the pool with her feet dangling over nothing, while her son EMMANUEL (40s, rumpled suit, a clipboard he has stopped looking at) paces the tiles, her granddaughter JOSÉPHINE (17, wet-weather parka, earbuds dangling) peels a strip of loose paint from the railing and flicks it into the void, and the surveyor TOMASZ KRUK (50s, hard hat under one arm, tape measure clipped to his belt) clears his throat twice before anyone looks at him.
Maman, they sign today. It is only a car park.
units.name: EMMANUEL

units.text: I taught you here. You held your breath nine seconds.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Madame, if I could just measure the deep end, we can--
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Nine seconds, Manu. And you came up crying.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Twelve feet, I think. Twelve and a half.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Marguerite pats the cold tile beside her, and Joséphine sits.
Tomasz winds the tape back slowly into its case.
